## Intent
Hypothesis: offloading walk1 (mask computation) to a Halide-generated kernel while keeping walk2 as a simple host scan can approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 10.888 at N=4000 to 6.583 at N=65000 — overhead amortization across the L2-resident regime (L1d spill at N≈949 sits below the smallest measured point). The L2→DRAM spill at N≈60787 produces no knee: ns/p rises only from 6.583 (N=65000) to 6.88 (N=4M), a 4.5% increase across a 60× working-set jump. Death rate raises the floor without reshaping the curve: at q=0.25 the plateau sits at 8.4–8.9 ns/p versus 6.6–6.9 at q=0.01, but the amortization-then-flat profile is identical. The absence of any spill knee confirms the algo is not streaming-limited.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 10.48 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 41.5% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. Bandwidth is flat across the L2→DRAM transition (10.48 at N=65000 vs 10.42 at N=262000), confirming compute/overhead-bound behavior rather than bandwidth-bound. Death rate erodes the peak to 8.19 GB/s (32.5%) at q=0.25 and to 7.77 GB/s at N=4M. The algo transitions from overhead-bound (N=4000, ~6 GB/s) to compute-bound (N≥16000, ~10 GB/s) but never approaches the streaming ceiling in any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the particle math — the histogram records 0 vector-suffixed instructions, and math uses scalar `fmul` (×4), `fadd` (×1), `fsub` (×1), `fcvtzs` (×5), and `csel` (×18). Walk1 is dispatched via `bl _halide_b3_mask`. The only SIMD appears in the walk2 mask scan: `ldp q1, q0` loads 32 mask bytes, then `orr.16b`/`ext.16b`/`orr.8b` reduces them to a `tst w8, #0xff` branch. The scatter is entirely byte-granular — 45 `ldrb`, 16 `strb`, 34 `cbz`, and 34 `bl` to `spawn` — with the spawn loop fully unrolled across 32 particles but each mask byte tested individually. This scalar, byte-granular codegen caps bandwidth at 42% of ceiling: `strb`/`ldrb` cannot fill cache lines, and the branchy per-particle respawn prevents streaming.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 10.48 GB/s (41.5% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=65000, and falls to 8.19 GB/s (32.5%) at q=0.25. The scalar codegen (0 vector instructions on particle math, byte-granular `strb`/`ldrb` scatter, 34 `bl` spawn calls) caps bandwidth far below the streaming ceiling regardless of death rate or N, so the Halide walk1 offload cannot compensate for the unvectorized simple walk2.
